-		Scenes are instantiated as children of the [TileMap] when it enters the tree. If you add/remove a scene tile in the [TileMap] that is already inside the tree, the [TileMap] will automatically instantiate/free the scene accordingly.
+		When placed on a [TileMapLayer], tiles from [TileSetScenesCollectionSource] will automatically instantiate an associated scene at the cell's position in the TileMapLayer.
body:
My opinion is that anytime the name of a class is explicitly mentioned, it should be a link. This is at least the case in the class reference.

Although, to go along with it, my _other_ opinion is we should avoid it in these cases, because:
> 	- AVOID using type tags when referencing to an instance of the type. This is especially notable when the type is very common (Color, Rect2, String, Node, Resource, etc.). It is _seriously_ annoying to read and harder to localize.
>		- "The [Color] of the light emitted by the [FogVolume]" -> "The color of the light emitted by the [FogVolume]"

Anyway, because this is an inconsistency present everywhere in the class reference, I don't really mind either way.
